q: Who was the first Secretary of the Railway Board in 1905:
e: N.G. Priestley was the first Secretary of the Railway Board when it was constituted in 1905. The Board was created to take over railway administration from the Public Works Department's Railway Branch, following the Thomas Robertson Committee's recommendations.

q: The GIP Railway Company (GIP) was incorporated in England by an Act of the British Parliament on:
e: 1st August 1849 — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: the Great Indian Peninsula (GIP) Railway Company was incorporated in England by an Act of the British Parliament on 1st August 1849. It was one of the earliest guaranteed railway companies in India. Related exam fact: the GIP Railway ran India's first passenger train in 1853 between Bombay and Thane. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: The formation of the Railway Board in 1905 was based upon the recommendations of:
e: Option (C) is correct: the Railway Board's formation in 1905 was based on the recommendations of the Thomas Robertson Committee. Robertson, appointed Special Commissioner for Indian Railways, recommended a dedicated board for railway administration. The Railway Board is the apex body of Indian Railways, exercising powers over policy, finance and administration for the whole system. Remember: Remember the underlying principle, not just the sentence: examiners often rephrase the same concept.

q: Before being brought under public ownership in 1951, at the time of Independence in 1947, there were:

options.A: 42 Railway Systems including 32 lines operated by Princely States
options.B: 37 Railway Systems with 10 lines operated by Princely States
options.C: 45 Railway Systems with 30 lines operated by Princely States
options.D: 32 Railway Systems with 25 lines operated by Princely States

e: 42 Railway Systems including 32 lines operated by Princely States — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: at Independence in 1947 there were 42 railway systems, including 32 lines operated by the princely states, before they were brought under public ownership and consolidated from 1951. The multiplicity of systems reflected fragmented private and state ownership. Related exam fact: the integration created the zonal railway system, beginning with the Southern Railway in 1951.

q: The Oak Grove School set up for the wards of Railway employees in 1888 is located in:
e: Option D (Jharipani, Mussoorie, Uttarakhand) is the correct choice. Option (D) is correct: the Oak Grove School, set up in 1888 for the wards of railway employees, is located at Jharipani, Mussoorie, Uttarakhand. It is among the oldest railway schools in India. Related exam fact: Oak Grove was established during the early expansion of railways in northern India to educate the children of employees posted at remote stations.

q: After independence and nationalization of Railway Zones, which was the only Railway Company which continued its private operations till 2016?
e: The correct answer is Central Provinces Railway Company. Option (B) is correct: the Central Provinces Railway Company was the only railway company that continued its private operations till 2016, long after other companies were nationalized and merged into the zonal system. Related exam fact: most private railway companies were taken over around Independence and consolidated into zones from 1951, making this company's survival exceptional.

q: The East India Railway Company’s first passenger train ran on 15th August 1854 covering a distance of 38 kms between:
e: Option (A) is correct: the East India Railway Company's first passenger train ran on 15th August 1854 between Howrah and Hooghly, covering 38 km. It was the second passenger train service in India after the Bombay-Thane run of 1853.
